title: "Social interactions & networks"
toc: true
---

## Motivation (stylized facts)
::: {.callout-note title="Stylized facts this mechanism aims to match"}
- Co-offending and clustering: offending is often socially embedded.
- Tactics and norms can diffuse through networks.
:::

## Mechanism
Peers affect behavior through:
- learning (information about opportunities, enforcement),
- complementarity (crime is easier or safer in groups),
- reputation and trust (partner choice),
- diffusion (new tactics spread).

## Canonical modeling primitives
- network structure (who meets whom)
- strategic complements vs substitutes in participation
- partner choice and betrayal risk
- dynamic learning and diffusion

## Predictions (qualitative)
- network clustering can amplify shocks (policy or opportunity changes)
- targeted interventions on central nodes can have outsized effects
- co-offending can be stable even when individual incentives are weak if complementarities are strong

## Later-on analysis
- connect to equilibrium selection: multiple stable participation levels
- connect to policing: enforcement on one node can displace to adjacent nodes (network displacement)
